title: quorum-policy/1
description: The trust decisions a verifier applies to a quorum/1 envelope. Every field is required: a policy with an omitted field would default to something, and a defaulted governance decision is how a gate becomes decoration.

policy_version.description: <label>+<identity>, where identity is the first 128 bits of sha256 over the canonical bytes of this document WITHOUT policy_version. Two materially different policies therefore cannot share one policy_version, and Q20_POLICY_IDENTITY recomputes it: the suffix is checked, not trusted. JSON Schema cannot compute a digest, so this pattern constrains only the SHAPE.

accepted_verdicts.description: The closed set of verdict tokens this policy recognises. Anything outside it is refused; there is no permissive default.

require_family_inequality.description: Cross-family review: author_family != reviewer_family. Settable to false only for a deliberately non-independent policy, and the verifier says so in its output.

require_family_trust.description: The MINIMUM trust level both families' evidence must reach. Under 'observed', an envelope carrying 'declared' evidence — which is what a yaml registry field is — fails closed.

require_evidence.description: When true the verifier must be handed the review evidence document and recompute its digest. Deleting the evidence then fails the check instead of skipping it.

require_residue_declaration.description: Require review.residue. Like every other require_* key this is MANDATORY to state — there is no permissive default, because a policy that is silent about residue is how a verdict quietly becomes a score again.
